episodes.title: Graphiti is advisory and mem0 remains active
episodes.summary: Graphiti/Neo4j is a shared operational/provenance graph layer for source-backed homelab and agent facts. It does not replace Hermes mem0 personal/preference memory unless Ben explicitly approves a later provider change.

facts.text: mem0 remains the active personal/preference memory provider; Graphiti is advisory operational provenance only.
facts.caveat: Policy fact; verify live Hermes configuration before changing any memory-provider setting.

episodes.title: Graphiti deployment posture is tori-local and non-public
episodes.summary: The reviewed production posture is a tori-local Graphiti + Neo4j deployment with no public route, loopback raw services, local Neo4j live data, and NAS used only for dumps, snapshots, manifests, and restore-test evidence.

facts.text: Raw Graphiti and Neo4j services must not be publicly exposed; agent access must go through the read-only wrapper.
facts.caveat: Deployment is still gated on Vaultwarden/BW unlock and reviewed preflight before live apply.

facts.text: Neo4j live data belongs on tori-local disk; NAS is for dumps, config snapshots, manifests, and restore-test evidence only.
facts.caveat: Do not infer current deployment state from this policy; inspect live host state before remediation.

episodes.title: Nippon qdevice dependency can deadlock NAS recovery
episodes.source_ref: homelab operations memory and recovery runbook
episodes.summary: The Nippon Proxmox cluster had a qdevice/qnetd dependency hosted at the NAS VM IP, creating a risk that the NAS VM cannot start when quorum depends on a service inside that VM path.

facts.text: Hosting qdevice/qnetd on cluster-dependent NAS VM infrastructure can deadlock quorum recovery and should be moved off that dependency path.
facts.caveat: Safety-critical; inspect current cluster quorum and qdevice state before taking action.

episodes.title: Vaultwarden homelab secrets convention
episodes.source_ref: Vaultwarden IaC import runbook and current homelab convention
episodes.summary: Homelab Git artifacts should store Vaultwarden folder/item/field references only. Ben selected his personal Vaultwarden vault with a flat folder named homelab and hierarchical item names for runtime secrets.

facts.text: Git should contain Vaultwarden references such as folder, item, and field names, never rendered secret values.
facts.caveat: Use runtime secret transport for actual values; do not paste credentials into Kanban comments, logs, dashboard JSON, or docs.

episodes.title: Jellyfin media stack stale NFS handle incident pattern
episodes.summary: A prior Jellyfin playback failure involved host NAS access being healthy while the long-running container saw stale NFS bind-mount handles. The safe diagnostic path compared host and container file access before restarting only the affected container after approval.

facts.text: For Jellyfin/media playback failures after NAS disruption, compare host path access with container bind-mount access before redesigning storage or deleting media.
facts.caveat: Historical incident pattern; inspect current host, container, and NAS state before remediation.
